A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GASS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–D are readable and support a complete comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and DrawBench generation experiments, quantitative comparisons and ablations, plus qualitative results and failure cases in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds quantitative prompt-length analysis, basis-selection controls and guidance-schedule comparisons.

M1.justification: The residual-axis search, spherical perturbation and re-normalization, and CLIP-gradient optimization remain unchanged. Appendix B's complete algorithm is identical. Added basis and scheduling experiments test configurations within the existing framework.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet and DrawBench with the same task coverage. v2 partitions existing DrawBench prompts by length; it does not introduce new prompts, datasets or input scenarios.

E2.justification: The main CFG, PG, CADS, IG and SPELL comparisons are retained. New Table 5 additionally evaluates isotropic perturbation (IP) and random-direction (RD) controls against GASS in the basis-selection comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation by prompt length: at most 8, 9–14 and at least 15 words, containing 92, 62 and 46 prompts. It also adds random-basis controls and an early-consecutive 10-step guidance condition. Main generation settings, backbones and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The diagnostic analyses expand substantially: Table 4 quantifies prompt-complexity effects previously illustrated qualitatively; Table 5 directly tests the chosen decomposition basis; and Table 6/Figure 6 compare guidance schedules and their visual effects. These address additional questions beyond v1's normalization, expansion-range and step-count ablations.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains mean and standard deviation across 1,000 ImageNet classes. Neither version supplies repeated-run uncertainty for the main comparisons, and the new analyses add no seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and existing ablation values are unchanged. Added results include prompt-length VS gains of 0.234/0.255/0.386, IP/RD CLIPScores of 0.308/0.313 versus GASS's 0.320, and VS/ImageReward of 8.215/0.808 for ten consecutive steps versus 8.127/0.757 for ten uniform steps. Figure 6 adds the lower-saturation observation, and Section 5.1 extends reported timing to 2.93–3.68 seconds for 10–20 guidance steps.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Proposition 4.1 and Appendix A's complete proof are unchanged. Algorithm 1 replaces v_i with e_i to match the already-existing Equation 3; this is a notation correction without new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about geometric disentanglement, controllable diversity enhancement and effectiveness across frozen backbones. The added experiments support existing claims without materially redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning perceived diversity versus metric trends across prompt lengths, the semantic-alignment benefit of the text-aligned basis, and schedule-dependent quality/alignment trade-offs. Appendix D's computational-overhead limitations and frozen-backbone failure explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository link, identifies the retained step-count experiments as uniform scheduling, specifies early-consecutive guidance, and expands A100 timing information. Appendix C's optimizer-independent baseline settings and implementation descriptions are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and substantive positioning remain unchanged. Berrada et al. becomes Ifriqi et al. for the same 'Entropy rectifying guidance for diffusion and flow models' reference, with the same title, coauthors and venue; this is a bibliographic change.

P1.justification: v2 adds explanatory paragraphs for the new analyses and makes localized wording, notation and citation edits. It also adds a conflict-of-interest disclosure, expands acknowledgements and updates the publication footer. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–5 and Figure 6, expands the former Table 4 into Table 6 with schedule labels and metric-direction arrows, and relocates Table 1 and Figures 4–5. Existing image examples and appendix displays are preserved, with corresponding renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the new basis controls, quantitative prompt-length breakdown and schedule comparison provide useful empirical support and clarify practical trade-offs. The code pointer and scheduling details also improve reproducibility information. These are bounded gains: the core method, main benchmark evidence and theory remain unchanged, while the new comparisons still lack repeated-run uncertainty.
